turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hi, I'm Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Mailingchoo.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Come on in, have a seat.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you tell me your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Adise Arkhafer,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: February 14, 2005.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Valentine's baby.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, Adise, what brings you in?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My acne.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I've had it since, like, 18, but the last six months it's gotten so much worse.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's on my face and some on my upper back.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What have you tried so far? I used a benzoyl peroxide wash, the ten percent one, for about a month, but I stopped it in the summer because it bleached all my towels and my pillowcases.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's really common. Did it help at all while you were using it? A little, I guess, not enough.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any medicines or supplements you take? I'm on the birth control pill, the norgestimate one, once a day,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: and vitamin D3, two thousand units a day.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any allergies to medications?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Amexicillin, I got hives all over when I was a kid.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: are your periods regular? Yes, pretty regular, on the pill anyway.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any extra hair growth on your chin or chest?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And does the acne leave scars or dark spots?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Dark spots, yeah, I don't think scars.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me take a look.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: On your forehead,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: cheeks and jawline you've got lots of open and closed cometones. so blackheads and whiteheads, about 15 red -inflamed bumps, and maybe 6 pustules. There are a few tender 4mm nodules along the jawline, no large cysts. You have some flat dark brown spots on both cheeks, that's post -inflammatory hyperpigmentation. I don't see any scarring. On the upper back, scattered red papules, maybe 10 or so.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So is it bad?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'd call this moderate acne vulgaris, with some dark spots from old breakouts. The good news is it's very treatable. I'd like to start two things.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: First,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: a Dapalene 0 .1 % gel, a pea -sized amount to your whole face at night. Start every other night for the first two weeks, because it can make your skin dry and a little peely.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Second, doxycycline 100 milligrams twice a day for three months. Take it with food and a full glass of water, and stay upright for 30 minutes after, so it doesn't irritate your esophagus. Keep it two hours away from dairy, calcium,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: or iron. Got it. Is it okay with my birth control? Yes, it doesn't make your pill less effective. Now,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: an important question.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is there any chance you could be pregnant right now? No, my last period was two weeks ago. But, um, if I did get pregnant, could I keep taking these?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No, and that's a really good question. Doxocycline can affect a baby's teeth and bones, and we don't use adaptiline in pregnancy either. So if you ever think you might be pregnant, stop both and call us.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, that makes sense.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The other big thing with doxycycline is sun sensitivity. You can burn really fast on it. So sunscreen, SPF 30 or higher every morning, and a hat if you're out a lot. The adaptiline makes you more sun sensitive too. I walk across campus all day at Lakeshore State, so I'll be careful.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Good. I'd also like you to go back to benzoyl peroxide, but the gentler four percent wash,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: once in the morning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It keeps bacteria from getting resistant to the antibiotic.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Use white towels and you won't care about the bleaching.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ah, okay. My roommate Priya was on a cutane last year and it totally cleared her up. Should I just do that?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's a stronger medicine we save for severe or scarring acne. me. Yours isn't there, so let's see how this does first. Which pharmacy do you use? The one on 4120 Belmont Avenue.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, I'll send both there, and a call back number. 555 -0118. Perfect.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It takes 8 to 12 weeks to see the full effect,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: so hang in there.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's see you back in 3 months.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: If you get a really bad sunburn,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: bad stomach upset, or headaches with vision changes on the doxycycline, stop it and call us. We'll do, thank you so much.
